contracts.name: Domain calls and events
contracts.contract: Exact domain/verb routing, serialized replies, structured errors and {name,data} event envelopes. Dedicated secret-bearing methods stay typed native operations.

contracts.name: Stable page identity
contracts.contract: Application tab IDs are stable strings; browser/strip/window IDs remain explicit native transport identifiers. Close/adopt/transfer and events resolve the owning tab.

contracts.name: Launch configuration
contracts.contract: Synchronous validated configuration, app-versus-test flags and Linux launch-switch implementation, with no Promise masquerading as a configuration object.

contracts.name: Profile authority
contracts.contract: Profile lookup and off-the-record lifetime, deliberate shared-data spaces, no fallback from private or isolated IDs to regular storage.

contracts.name: Canonical documents
contracts.contract: Profile/document revisions, identity-aware reconciliation, tombstones, canonical notifications and debounce/write close barrier.

contracts.name: Page-message substrate
contracts.contract: Bounded authenticated routing, document lifetime, trusted shell distinction and narrow evaluation. F25 needs only scroll reporting, not the entire selection/peek UI.

contracts.name: Protected secrets
contracts.contract: Linux protected credential storage and real OS authentication before reveal/export/secret writes. Metadata, parsers and non-secret controls can proceed earlier.

contracts.name: Policy protection state
contracts.contract: Reliable media/capture/PiP/prompt/dirty-input/visible-pane state before automatic freezing/discard is enabled. Unknown state protects the page.

contracts.name: Filesystem and drag
contracts.contract: Owned native file tokens, validated paths, picker cancellation and native export/drop sessions. DOM URLs/text and native files are distinct.

contracts.name: Window lifecycle
contracts.contract: Close request/acknowledgment, readiness, requested focus versus observed activation, compositor-appropriate geometry. R02 consumes target identities without assuming Wayland global coordinates.

contracts.name: Effective shortcuts
contracts.contract: One Linux binding/default/alias/conflict catalog shared by native dispatch, command hints and Settings. Preserve physical modifier identities.

contracts.name: Service authority
contracts.contract: Define app-wide, profile-wide and renderer-local ownership so extra native windows do not duplicate services or writers.

findings.title: Find, Print, Save Page and DevTools are exposed but cannot execute
findings.impact: Ctrl+F opens a search bar that cannot search a native page. Print, system print, Save Page, DevTools, Inspect and Console actions reject instead of completing.
findings.evidence: Shared FindBar still calls find/stopFinding and command dispatch calls print/runPageCommand/showDevTools. Linux HostWebView forwards them as tab.command, whose native dispatcher still lacks these methods. Linux shortcuts consume matched accelerators, preventing normal Chromium shortcut fallback. Domain migration does not supply per-tab commands.
findings.caveat: Source revalidated after rebase; current UI cannot be runtime-tested until N01/N02/N03/N04 bootstrap compatibility is repaired. Chromium context-menu alternatives may exist.
findings.verify: On a loaded native page, search for known text, print, save and open each DevTools mode. Require a successful visible result, not merely a dispatched command.
findings.proof: Current-source revalidation; pre-rebase runtime evidence is historical
suggested_steps: Implement typed per-tab find, print/system-print/save-page and DevTools modes using Chromium helpers.
Emit find results and preserve tab ownership, cancellation and native modal shortcut ownership.
acceptance: Find known text with counts, previous/next and dismissal on two real tabs.
Print/save and all DevTools modes produce actual correct-tab results from shell and page focus.

issue.title: [Linux parity F01] [P1] Find, Print, Save Page and DevTools are exposed but cannot execute

findings.title: The default isolated-profile flow and private windows are unsupported
findings.impact: A user can create and select an isolated profile whose real pages and services fail to load. New Incognito Window updates shell state but cannot create its native window.
findings.evidence: The isolated-profile default still creates generated profile IDs; the Linux resolver permits only empty/default identities for native tabs, services and regular windows and rejects incognito. No upstream commit adds Linux profile ownership.
findings.caveat: Sharing default engine data can work as spaces. This is unsupported behavior, not demonstrated cross-profile leakage. Rebased source review at 8b165bd5; N01 prevents a fresh Linux UI from building, so prior native/adapter reproductions are historical evidence rather than a runtime result on this revision.
findings.verify: Create an independent profile and browse in it; create a private window; then test cookie, history and storage isolation, disposal and restart exclusion.
findings.proof: Current-source revalidation; pre-rebase runtime evidence is historical
suggested_steps: Add a Linux Profile/OTR registry and route tabs, services, windows and adoption through it.
Capability-gate unsupported profiles/private controls until implementation; never substitute the regular profile.
Reconcile failed native creation with shell state.
acceptance: Independent profiles isolate cookies, history, localStorage and extensions; shared-data profiles share deliberately.
Private windows create real OTR pages, clear on disposal and never persist.
Cross-profile adoption rejects and failed creation leaves no phantom window.

findings.impact: Ardia’s site panel gives incorrect connection information and cannot show the expected certificate or mixed-content details.
findings.evidence: SiteControls still asks getSecurityInfo; Linux has no command or security event producer. Security remains null, which SiteConnection converts to Local Page and local/internal description for an ordinary HTTP/HTTPS page.
findings.caveat: This is incorrect Ardia presentation, not evidence of a TLS validation bypass. Runtime recheck waits on bootstrap migration.
findings.verify: Compare the site panel on HTTPS, HTTP, mixed content, an invalid certificate and an internal page. Unknown security must not be labeled local.
findings.proof: Current-source revalidation; pre-rebase runtime evidence is historical
suggested_steps: Observe native security state and implement getSecurityInfo with the current public schema.
Render unknown/unavailable honestly and invalidate old certificate state on navigation.
acceptance: Check HTTPS, HTTP, mixed content, invalid certificate and internal pages.
Unknown never renders local and previous-document certificates cannot persist.

findings.title: Live-folder and Calendar edits can stay stale, disappear or overwrite another window
findings.impact: A setting changed in the utility window does not reach an already open browser. Later whole-document saves can restore deleted folders or overwrite preferences. Closing Settings before its debounce expires can lose the edit.
findings.evidence: live.json moved into state/live and gained versioned JSON serialization; it still loads one module-local store and writes whole snapshots after 800ms. Linux caches remain per-renderer, document writes have no broadcast/merge, and utility close flushes only session persistence.
findings.caveat: Schema versioning does not fix stale caches or concurrent whole-document overwrites. Pre-rebase adapter reproduction showed disk/Settings false and browser cache true. Rebased source review at 8b165bd5; N01 prevents a fresh Linux UI from building, so prior native/adapter reproductions are historical evidence rather than a runtime result on this revision.
findings.verify: Open two browser windows and Settings; edit/delete a live folder and a Calendar preference; close immediately and after 800 ms; change the peer window; restart and compare all copies.
findings.proof: Current-source revalidation; pre-rebase runtime evidence is historical
suggested_steps: Define revisioned document snapshots, canonical updates and identity-aware live-folder merge/tombstones.
Update host caches and live stores across renderers without echo writes.
Register pending document timers/writes with save-before-close; retain live.json version and migration metadata.
acceptance: Two browser windows and Settings converge after preference edits and folder creation/deletion.
Close immediately and after 800ms; restart preserves the same final state.
Concurrent edits survive; save failures retain the utility for retry.

Authentication denied/cancelled/expired never reveals secrets; inspect encryption at rest.

findings.title: Cross-window dragging has coordinate and per-renderer state risks
findings.impact: A tab dragged outside its window could miss its target, create a wrongly positioned window or lose the intended insertion position.
findings.evidence: Window-drop helper moved to state/drag and still computes bottom-up screen y while Linux returns gfx top-down bounds. Drag state/resolvers remain module-local across separate renderers. Native previews remain unavailable; upstream now calls preview helpers unconditionally.
findings.caveat: Original physical cross-window failure remains a risk, not a confirmed desktop repro. Explicit native adoption and same-window reorder have paths. New unconditional calls are a separate source-confirmed compatibility hazard. Rebased source review at 8b165bd5; N01 prevents a fresh Linux UI from building, so prior native/adapter reproductions are historical evidence rather than a runtime result on this revision.
findings.verify: Drag within and between two windows on monitors with different origin/scale; drop into a specific row, outside all windows, and cancel during transfer.
findings.proof: Current-source revalidation; pre-rebase runtime evidence is historical

Define Linux coordinate/target-identity and native DnD session contracts; broker across renderers.
Provide optional-helper fallback/capability gating; do not treat y inversion as sufficient on Wayland.

findings.title: Window focus/frame/fullscreen bookkeeping lacks native notifications
findings.impact: The shared focused-window state and saved frame may stay stale after compositor activation, movement/resizing or fullscreen transitions.
findings.evidence: Native window bookkeeping moved behind WindowPort onEvent; it still needs focus/frame/fullScreen notifications. Linux still emits none and its bounds observer only relayouts the overlay. Restoring old bounds is not evidence of recording user changes.
findings.caveat: Keep as a desktop verification risk until comparing actual compositor, store and session. Chromium can independently restore native placement. Rebased source review at 8b165bd5; N01 prevents a fresh Linux UI from building, so prior native/adapter reproductions are historical evidence rather than a runtime result on this revision.
findings.verify: Move/resize/focus two windows and toggle fullscreen through the compositor; inspect store values, saved session and post-restart actual bounds.
findings.proof: Current-source revalidation; pre-rebase runtime evidence is historical
